Hi Marta,

Thanks again for the call today. Two quick follow-ups so procurement has what it needs:

1) We need a formal statement on whether Geofence.AI can guarantee full multi-region failover (RTO/RPO) when failover is constrained by geofencing regulations (i.e., customer-subnet pinned to EU jurisdiction). Specifically, our customer is requesting:
   - RTO <= 15 minutes for control-plane failover to warm standby (EU->EU)
   - RPO <= 1 hour for replicated model state and cache

2) If the above cannot be guaranteed for geofenced subnets due to routing/peering limitations, can you confirm the carveout language you propose (acceptable scope, metrics, and any financial remediation)?

I attached the redline (geofence-sla-redlines.pdf) and a simplified topology showing the constrained interconnects (eu-network-topology.png). Can procurement return a proposed contract clause and a short paragraph we can show the customer by EOD Wednesday?

Short deadline — customer legal wants an explicit clause before the PO. If we need a technical runbook from CloudX to validate warm-standby activation time, please loop ops@cloudx.com into one thread.

Thanks,

Hi Kimberly,

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers from my side after checking with NetOps and Legal:

- Geofence.AI can commit to warm-standby activation within 15 minutes for intra-EU failover in the majority of topologies we support, but there are two caveats:
  1) If the customer's tenancy enforces a hard geofence at the ISP/edge (no cross-border egress allowed), automated model replication across regions is blocked. In those cases we can offer manual intervention-based failover with RTO up to 4 hours.
  2) For RPO, we can guarantee <=1h when asynchronous replication is permitted through our private peering. If peering uses customer-managed edge devices with strict firewall rules, RPO may slide to 3-6 hours.

We propose the following carveout language (high-level):
"Failover and data replication SLAs are subject to third-party network routing and customer-managed edge controls. Where cross-border egress is restricted by law or customer policy, Geofence.AI will provide documented manual failover procedures; automated failover guarantees (RTO/RPO) do not apply. Financial remediation shall be limited to a service credit capped at 10% of monthly service fees for the affected scope."

I'll have Procurement draft a more formal clause. We will also request CloudX to provide a runbook/confirmation on peering timelines — looping them here added.

Best,
Marta

Thanks for the context. I agree with a customer-facing paragraph that is explicit and non-technical: explain that automated cross-border failover is limited when edge policies prevent egress, list the manual failover option and the paid dedicated peering path with associated lead-times.
